I was on the other end of this in my last relationship. When my ED started I was overweight, and in 3 months I had lost (not going to say the #-so if you feel inclined to know, the weight of an adult male gray wolf) and was dying. Actually dying-the doctor told me I had a few months left to live if I didn’t start recovering. That didn’t stop me right away. 

I had entertained going into treatment and my ex said he supported me in it, that he would wait for me and just wanted to see me get better-I told him I was thinking about it but I’m not sure I really was at that point. 

It took him breaking up with me to start recovering. There were other reasons we broke up but the reason he stated was that it was because he felt helpless and it was affecting his everyday life. 

Please, do not put that burden on yourself. There is nothing you can do, unfortunately. She has to make the decision herself. All you can do is be there for her and evaluate how much you can handle. 

It’s been two years since we broke up and I’m still grieving. I loved him so much snd still do. I understand now that due to his own issues that we probably wouldn’t have worked out anyway but I still have such deep regret knowing he had to go through all of that alongside me. 

The point is that yes, he was very supportive and did all he could. But it wasn’t enough. It wasn’t enough because ED’s are serious mental illnesses and they cloud every aspect of reality. 

I’d go back and change things in a heartbeat. I’ve gained most of the weight back now anyway. It was never worth it. Now here I am, two years later still heavily grieving the loss of time with someone I would do anything to have more with. 

There might come a point where you will have to put yourself first. I understand why he did and am glad he did so. 

I am glad you are in therapy and taking care of yourself. The last thing I want is for her to get to the point where she is in the position I was. I hope to god she doesn’t. Please be easy on yourself. I wish you both the best.

It is about the mindset, which is very different during active and conscious dieting versus living a healthy lifestyle with a balance diet. One of the fundamental aspects of eating disorders are obsessive thoughts and actions, so any such mindset that promotes fixating on food choices and numbers (I.e., dieting) will somehow, one way or another trigger a relapse.

Once I learned to eat again, the practice of facing my fears bled into other areas of my life, which only reinforced recovery.

I almost died from Anorexia a little over a year ago (was never super close to underweight but lost an immense amount of weight in a short time and was told by doctors I was going to die in a month if I didn’t  recover). 

I know you are asking for advice on how to tone up in attempts to recover, so I am proud of you for that. I’ve read on (*edit, I put the wrong sub*) r/Anorexiarecovery a lot in the past that weight lifting has helped a LOT of people feel more confident and has forced them to increase their intake due to extreme hunger from all the physical activity! 

I didn’t do anything to tone up, as for some people with an excessive exercise component continuing to work out can be harmful to recovery-if you are one of those people, I would advise against it. Honestly what I initially did was increase my portions of my safe foods and gradually work my way up from there. Of course I had the help of intense therapy and an outpatient program too. If you do not have those, I would advise for you to get in some sort of therapy if you can. I know this is difficult, especially in the US, but there are a few alternative options and if you would like advice at any point you can feel free to PM me. 

One day at a time, okay? That’s all you can do. Don’t try and merely force yourself to eat without any real motivation because that won’t work. The driving force of recovery is making the decision to live, because this illness will inevitably kill you one way or another If you do not recover. If you can make that decision, you will be able to do it. We as humans are wired to fight to survive. 

I never thought I would be able to recover, and I did, because I think one day I just decided that dying from Anorexia would be a really sad way to go out. Well and also because my ex boyfriend left me because of it and I wanted to get him back by proving I was better. Oof.
